sentences.en: For my project on invertebrates, I chose to study tardigrades.
sentences.zh: 在我的无脊椎动物项目中，我选择了研究水熊虫。

sentences.en: These are microscopic - or to be more precise - near-microscopic animals.
sentences.zh: 这些是微观的——或者更准确地说——接近微观的动物。

sentences.en: There are well over a thousand known species of these tiny animals, which belong to the phylum Tardigrada.
sentences.zh: 目前已知的这类微小动物有上千种以上，它们属于缓步动物门（Tardigrada）。

sentences.en: Most tardigrades range in length from 0.05 to 1 millimetre, though the largest species can grow to be 1.2 millimetres in length.
sentences.zh: 大多数水熊虫体长在0.05至1毫米之间，尽管最大的种类体长可达1.2毫米。

sentences.en: They are also sometimes called 'water bears': 'water' because that's where they thrive best, and 'bear' because of the way they move.
sentences.zh: 它们有时也被称为‘水熊’：‘水’是因为它们最适宜在水中生存，‘熊’则源于其移动方式。

sentences.en: 'Moss piglet' is another name for tardigrades because of the way they look when viewed from the front.
sentences.zh: ‘苔藓猪仔’是水熊虫的另一个名称，源于从正面观察时它们的外形。

sentences.en: They were first discovered in Germany in 1773 by Johann Goeze, who coined the name Tardigrada.
sentences.zh: 它们于1773年在德国首次被约翰·戈泽（Johann Goeze）发现，他创造了‘Tardigrada’这一名称。

sentences.en: As I say, there are many different species of tardigrade - too many to describe here - but, generally speaking, the different species share similar physical traits.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，水熊虫有众多不同物种——多到此处无法一一描述——但总体而言，不同物种具有相似的生理特征。

sentences.en: They have a body which is short, and also rounded - a bit like barrel - and the body comprises four segments.
sentences.zh: 它们的身体短而圆润，略呈桶状，身体由四个体节组成。

sentences.en: Each segment has a pair of legs, at the end of which are between four and eight sharp claws.
sentences.zh: 每个体节上都有一对腿，腿末端长有4至8个尖锐的爪子。

sentences.en: I should also say that some species don't have any claws; what they have are discs, and these work by means of suction.
sentences.zh: 我还需说明，有些物种完全没有爪子；它们长有吸盘，依靠吸力发挥作用。

sentences.en: They enable the tardigrade to cling on to surfaces or to grip its prey.
sentences.zh: 这些结构使水熊虫能够附着在物体表面或抓住猎物。

sentences.en: Within the body, there are no lungs, or any organs for breathing at all.
sentences.zh: 其体内没有肺，也完全没有任何呼吸器官。

sentences.en: Instead, oxygen and also blood are transported in a fluid that fills the cavity of the body.
sentences.zh: 相反，氧气和血液通过充满体腔的一种液体进行输送。

sentences.en: Audioscripts As far as the tardigrade's head is concerned, the best way l can describe this is that it looks rather strange - a bit squashed even - though many of the websites I looked at described its appearance as cute, which isn't exactly very scientific.
sentences.zh: 就水熊虫的头部而言，我所能做的最好描述是：它看起来相当奇特——甚至有点扁平——尽管我查阅的许多网站将其外观描述为‘可爱’，这显然并不十分科学。

sentences.en: The tardigrade's mouth is a kind of tube that can open outwards to reveal teeth-like structures known as 'stylets'.
sentences.zh: 水熊虫的口器是一种管状结构，可向外张开，露出类似牙齿的构造，称为‘口针’。

sentences.en: These are sharp enough to pierce plant or animal cells.
sentences.zh: 这些口针足够锋利，能刺穿植物或动物细胞。

sentences.en: So, where are tardigrades found?
sentences.zh: 那么，水熊虫分布于何处？

sentences.en: Well, they live in every part of the world, in a variety of habitats: most commonly, on the bed of a lake, or on many kinds of plants or in very wet environments.
sentences.zh: 它们遍布全球各类生境：最常见的是栖息于湖泊底部、多种植物表面，或极其潮湿的环境中。

sentences.en: There's been some interesting research which has found that tardigrades are capable of surviving radiation and very high pressure, and they're also able to withstand temperatures as cold as -200 degrees centigrade, or highs of more than 148 degrees centigrade, which is incredibly hot.
sentences.zh: 一些有趣的研究发现，水熊虫能够耐受辐射和极高压力，并且可承受低至零下200摄氏度、高至148摄氏度以上的极端温度，后者可谓极其酷热。

sentences.en: t has been said that tardigrades could survive long after human beings have been wiped out, even in the event of an asteroid hitting the earth.
sentences.zh: 有人称，即使人类因小行星撞击地球而彻底灭绝，水熊虫仍可能长期存活下去。

sentences.en: If conditions become too extreme and tardigrades are at risk of drying out, they enter a state called cryptobiosis.
sentences.zh: 当环境变得过于极端、水熊虫面临脱水风险时，它们会进入一种名为‘隐生状态’（cryptobiosis）的生理状态。

sentences.en: They curl into a a ball, called a tun - that's T-U-N - by retracting their head and legs, and their metabolism drops to less than one percent of normal levels.
sentences.zh: 它们将头部和腿缩回，蜷缩成一个球状结构，称为‘桶状体’（tun，拼写为T-U-N），此时新陈代谢速率降至正常水平的百分之一以下。

sentences.en: They can remain like this until they are re-introduced to water, when they will come back to life in a matter of a few hours.
sentences.zh: 它们可长期维持此状态，直至重新接触水分，数小时内即可复苏并恢复生命活动。

sentences.en: While in a state of cryptobiosis, tardigrades produce a protein that protects their DNA.
sentences.zh: 处于隐生状态时，水熊虫会产生一种保护其DNA的蛋白质。

sentences.en: In 2016, scientists revived two tardigrades that had been tuns for more than 30 years.
sentences.zh: 2016年，科学家成功复活了两只已处于桶状体状态逾30年的水熊虫。

sentences.en: There was a report that, in 1948, a 120-year-old tun was revived, but this experiment has never been repeated.
sentences.zh: 曾有报道称，1948年一只已有120年历史的桶状体被成功复活，但该实验至今未被重复验证。

sentences.en: There are currently several tests taking place in space, to determine how long tardigrades might be.
sentences.zh: 目前正开展多项太空实验，以测定水熊虫在太空环境中可能存活的时间。

sentences.en: able to survive there.
sentences.zh: 它们在太空中能够存活多久。

sentences.en: I believe the record so far is 10 days.
sentences.zh: 据信迄今最长纪录为10天。

sentences.en: So, erm, moving on.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，接下来我们继续。

sentences.en: In terms of their diet, tardigrades consume liquids in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 就食性而言，水熊虫靠摄取液体维持生存。

sentences.en: Although they have teeth, they don't use these for chewing.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们拥有牙齿，却并不用于咀嚼。

sentences.en: They suck the juices from.
sentences.zh: 它们吸食……

sentences.en: moss, or extract fluid from seaweed, but some species prey on other tardigrades, from other species or within their own.
sentences.zh: 苔藓汁液，或从海藻中提取体液，但某些物种会捕食其他种类乃至同种的水熊虫。

sentences.en: I suppose this isn't surprising, given that tardigrades are mainly comprised of liquid and are coated with a type of gel.
sentences.zh: 考虑到水熊虫主要由液体构成，且体表覆盖一层凝胶状物质，这一点或许并不令人意外。

sentences.en: Finally, I'd like to mention the conservation status of tardigrades.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想提一下水熊虫的保护现状。

sentences.en: It is estimated that they have been In existence for approximately half a billion years and, in that time, they have survived five mass extinctions.
sentences.zh: 据估计，它们已在地球上存在约五亿年，在此期间成功经历了五次大规模生物灭绝事件。

sentences.en: So, it will probably come as no surprise to you, that tardigrades have not been evaluated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and are not on any endangered list.
sentences.zh: 因此，水熊虫尚未被国际自然保护联盟（IUCN）评估，也未被列入任何濒危物种名录，想必大家不会感到意外。

sentences.en: Some researchers have described them as thriving.
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员甚至形容它们正处于繁盛状态。

sentences.en: Does anyone have any questions they'd like to ask?
sentences.zh: 有没有人有什么问题想要提问？
